summary: Vilgelm Mikhailovich Berner (1903–1958) was an Indology scholar who studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute in 1931. From 1935 to 1936, he served as an aspirant at the Institute of Anthropology, Moscow State University.

Vilhelm Peter Grønbech (1873–1948) studied at the University of Copenhagen (1890–1897) under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Holger Pedersen. A religious studies and linguistics scholar, he was docent at Copenhagen (1908, 1911) and taught at Danmarks Lærerhøjskole (1912–1919).

Linguist and Iranian/Central Asian specialist Vilhelm Thomsen (1842–1927) studied at the University of Copenhagen under Johan Nicolai Madvig and Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He served as professor at Copenhagen (1887–1913) and chairman of the Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters (1876–1927).

Vilhelm Trenckner (1824–1891), an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar, studied at the University of Copenhagen in 1841 under Johan Nicolai Madvig, Christian Thorning Engelstoft Hermansen, and Niels Ludvig Westergaard. In 1860, he taught at Det Kgl. Vajsenhus.

Ville Husgafvel is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki (2015–2023) and visited SOAS (2017–2018). He worked as a project researcher at the University of Helsinki from 2022 to 2023.

Vimla Karnatak is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar. As attested in 2000, she served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University.

Vinay Lal (born 1961), a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1980 to 1982. Around 1993, he became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at UCLA.

Vinaya Kshirsagar is an Indology and linguistics scholar who served as a professor at Dr. D. Y. Patil Medical College, Hospital & Research Centre in 2015. She is attested as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary at Deccan College in 2026.

Vincenc Lesný (1882–1953) studied at Charles University, Oxford, and Bonn under Josef Zubatý, Moriz Winternitz, Arthur Anthony Macdonell, and Hermann Jacobi. An Indologist, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar, he served as professor at Charles University starting in 1924.

Vincenc Pořízka (1905–1982) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Palacký University and Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Otakar Pertold. He served as Professor of Hindi at Charles University (1951) and taught at Humboldt University (1960–1967).

Vincent Arthur Smith (1848–1920) was an Indology and history scholar educated at Trinity College Dublin and Cambridge. He worked in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900), read Indian history at Dublin and Oxford, and curated the Indian Institute, Oxford (ca. 1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem (born 1970) is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Leiden University (MA, PhD), Taisho, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities, and under Lucia Dolce. He was attested as a research fellow at Leiden University in 2012.

Vincent Eltschinger (born 1970), specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Lausanne under Tom Tillemans and at Vienna. He served as research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and became directeur d’études at EPHE around 2015.

Vincent Goossaert (born 1969), a scholar of sinology and religious studies, studied under Kristofer Schipper. He worked at the CNRS (ca. 1998–2012) and became Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.

Vincent Lefèvre is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied under Bruno Dagens at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He has served as a curator at the Guimet Museum.

Vincent Tournier, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at EPHE and Leiden under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub and Seishi Karashima. His posts include Maître de conférences at Sciences Po Grenoble and professor positions at EFEO, Göttingen, and the University of Tokyo.

Vincenz Scherzl (1843–1906) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Charles University, Saint Petersburg under Kaetan Kossovich, King's College London, and Moscow State University. He served as professor of comparative linguistics at Kharkiv (1880–1885) and Odesa (1885–1906).
Vincenzo Vergiani is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raffaele Torella. In 2007, he was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge.

Vinit Deo is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy who earned an external MA in Indology from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2022–2024). He was an alumnus at Indira Gandhi National Open University in 2024.

Vinod Kumar Roy is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at Patna University, the University of Delhi (BA 1990, PhD 2003), and Magadh University. In 2019, he served as Assistant Professor (Senior Scale) at Magadh University.
